item.title: Informe desde Sarajevo: Bosnia elige, entre el nacionalismo y el giro proeuropeo
item.description: Cierra la jornada electoral en Bosnia-Herzegovina, donde los datos casi definitivos arrojan dos fotografías muy distintas: por un lado, el grupo bosniaco musulmán eligió al candidato más proeuropeo como su representante para la presidencia tripartita, mientras que croatas y serbobosnios se decantaron por candidatos más nacionalistas. La jornada electoral también estuvo marcada por la baja participación, de alrededor del 40%, unos 10 puntos menos que en los anteriores comicios generales de 2022. item.title: Man’s $3 Goodwill painting turns out to be a 1650 Flemish work worth $190,000
item.description: In a remarkable twist of fate, a former antiques dealer purchased a painting for just $3, suspecting it held greater value. Appraisers on Antiques Roadshow estimated its worth between $20,000 and $30,000, but the auction result astonished everyone, fetching $190,000. This stunning Flemish piece, dating back to around 1650, serves as a testament to the hidden gems that can be discovered in thrift shops and donation centers. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Meet Nathan, the Texas seventh-grader who turned shellfish waste into a water-cleaning project
item.description: Nathan Gael Montelongo, a seventh-grader from La Joya, Texas, created a project using chitosan. He collected discarded shellfish shells to produce chitosan powder and tested its effectiveness on polluted water. Studies showed that chitosan improved water clarity and benefited zebrafish embryos in experiments. Nathan designed a prototype raft that could automate water quality monitoring and treatment. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
